title: Geesink fait pleurer le Japon (Tokyo 1964)
style: Claymation 3D render: handmade plasticine / modeling-clay figurines with visible fingerprints and soft clay texture, miniature diorama set, tilt-shift shallow depth of field, warm cinematic lighting, rich saturated colors, stop-motion animation look. Never photorealistic, no real photos, no archival look, no black-and-white. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark. Vertical 9:16 composition, main subject in the upper and middle part of the frame, lower quarter kept simple.

geesink.name: Anton Geesink
geesink.description: Dutch judoka clay figurine: a giant, extremely tall, broad-shouldered heavyweight man around 30 years old, much taller than everyone else, short slicked-back blond hair, square jaw, light blue eyes, calm serious expression, very large hands. Wears a thick white cotton judogi with a black belt and a small Netherlands flag patch (red, white, blue horizontal stripes) on the left chest.

kaminaga.name: Akio Kaminaga
kaminaga.description: Japanese judoka clay figurine: stocky and powerful man around 28 years old, clearly shorter than Geesink (his head reaches Geesink's shoulders), short cropped black hair, thick black eyebrows, proud determined expression. Wears a white judogi with a black belt and a small Japan flag patch (white with a red circle) on the left chest.

officiels.name: Officiels néerlandais
officiels.description: Three middle-aged Dutch official clay figurines in dark 1960s suits with bright orange ties, white shirts and polished black leather dress shoes, one bald with glasses, one with a grey moustache, one with combed brown hair.

arbitre.name: Arbitre
arbitre.description: Japanese judo referee clay figurine, middle-aged, neat black hair, wearing a dark navy blazer, white shirt, dark tie and grey trousers.

lines.text: En {1964|mille neuf cent soixante-quatre}, un géant néerlandais a fait pleurer tout le Japon.

shots.image: Dramatic low-angle wide shot at dusk: the giant Geesink figurine stands like a colossus over a miniature clay Tokyo cityscape from the 1960s, tiny houses and a red-and-white lattice tower reaching only his knees, orange sky, strong backlight.
Extreme close-up of Geesink's face looking down at the camera, calm and serious, strong square jaw, warm rim light, dark arena background.
Close-up of a Japanese spectator figurine in a 1960s dark suit crying, big glossy clay tears rolling down his cheeks, blurred packed stadium crowd behind.

lines.text: Tokyo. Pour la première fois, le judo entre aux Jeux olympiques. Chez lui, au Japon.

shots.image: Miniature clay diorama of Tokyo in 1964 on a bright sunny morning: Mount Fuji with a snowy cap in the background, cherry blossom trees, colorful festive bunting flags, a large modern stadium in the center.
A pristine green-and-beige tatami judo mat on a raised platform under a single spotlight in an empty arena, five interlocking colored clay rings hanging above it.

Exterior of the Nippon Budokan made of clay: octagonal hall with a sweeping temple-like roof topped with a golden ornament, crowds of tiny Japanese figurines walking in, Japanese flags (white with a red circle) waving.

lines.text: Les Japonais gagnent trois catégories sur quatre.

shots.image: Three Japanese judoka figurines in white judogi standing proudly on three podium steps, each holding up a shiny gold medal, golden confetti falling, joyful smiles.
Close-up of a wooden display case with four velvet slots: three hold shiny clay gold medals, the fourth slot on the right is empty and lit by a spotlight.

lines.text: Il ne reste que la plus prestigieuse : toutes catégories.

shots.image: A single huge gold medal resting on a red velvet cushion under one dramatic spotlight in a dark arena, dust particles floating in the light beam.

Line-up of judoka figurines of very different sizes standing side by side on a tatami, from a small lightweight to a huge heavyweight, the last and tallest one is Geesink, open weight category feeling.

lines.text: En finale, le champion japonais Akio Kaminaga.

shots.image: Heroic low-angle shot: Kaminaga walking out of a tunnel into the bright Budokan arena, packed stands of Japanese spectators waving small Japanese flags.
Medium close-up of Kaminaga tightening his black belt with both hands, fierce focused eyes, crowd blurred behind.

lines.text: Face à lui, Anton {Geesink|Guésink}. {1,98 m|un mètre quatre-vingt-dix-huit}. {120 kilos|cent vingt kilos}.

shots.image: Extreme low-angle shot of Geesink stepping onto the tatami, towering and intimidating, arena ceiling lights glowing behind his head.
Kaminaga and Geesink figurines standing side by side in front of a wooden height measuring chart with plain tick marks, Geesink is a full head taller, Kaminaga looks up at him.
Geesink standing on an old-fashioned mechanical floor scale, the needle swung to the far end, the scale slightly bending under his weight, humorous touch.

lines.text: {Geesink|Guésink} l'emmène au sol et l'immobilise. {30|Trente} secondes plus tard… ippon.

shots.image: Dynamic action shot: Geesink throwing Kaminaga down onto the tatami, both figurines caught mid-motion, a puff of clay dust, dramatic tilted angle.
Top-down view: Geesink pinning Kaminaga on his back on the tatami with a scarf hold (kesa-gatame), Kaminaga straining to escape, drops of sweat.
The referee figurine thrusting his arm straight up to the sky to announce ippon, Geesink still holding Kaminaga on the mat below, explosive burst of light behind the referee.

lines.text: Le Budokan devient silencieux. Dans les tribunes, des Japonais pleurent.

shots.image: Wide shot of the packed Budokan stands, thousands of tiny Japanese spectator figurines completely frozen and silent, cold dim bluish light.
Close-up of Japanese spectators in the stands crying, a woman in a kimono covering her mouth with her hand, men with glossy clay tears.
An elderly Japanese man in a 1960s suit wiping a tear with a white handkerchief, soft melancholic light.

lines.text: Les officiels néerlandais veulent courir sur le tapis pour fêter ça. Avec leurs chaussures.

shots.image: The three Dutch officials leaping up from their bench, arms raised in joy, mouths wide open shouting.
The three Dutch officials running toward the tatami in excitement, ties flying, the judo mat in the foreground.
Floor-level extreme close-up: a polished black leather dress shoe with an orange sock, about to step onto the edge of the sacred tatami mat, dramatic tension.

lines.text: {Geesink|Guésink} les arrête d'un geste. Et il salue son adversaire.

shots.image: Geesink kneeling on the tatami raising one open hand firmly toward the camera to stop the officials, calm authoritative face, the three officials frozen mid-run in the background.
Geesink and Kaminaga standing face to face on the tatami, bowing deeply to each other, respectful atmosphere, warm golden light.
Close-up of Geesink's huge hand and Kaminaga's hand in a firm handshake, white judogi sleeves, black belts visible, warm light.

lines.text: Ce jour-là, le judo est devenu un sport mondial.

shots.image: A clay globe of the Earth on a wooden stand, tiny judoka figurines in white judogi standing on every continent and bowing.
Children of many different origins in white judogi practicing on a tatami in a bright modern dojo, many small colorful national flags hanging on the wall, joyful.

lines.text: Abonne-toi pour plus d'histoires Hors Limite.

shots.image: Geesink and Kaminaga figurines standing side by side on a tatami with arms crossed, looking at the camera, big empty dark wall in the upper part of the frame, dramatic red and gold lighting.
